nav.heartClock: Heart clock: ECG and the cardiac cycle
heartClock.title: Heart clock
heartClock.intro: One timer drives the whole cardiac cycle. The ECG below is generated from it: change the heart rate and watch the waves and the phases of the cycle follow.
heartClock.ecgLabel: Synthetic ECG, one lead. Grid: 25 mm per second, 10 mm per millivolt.
heartClock.schematic: A schematic teaching model, not a recording and not for diagnosis. Not reviewed by a physician. Durations follow published averages and are simplified; some values are model assumptions.
heartClock.wiggers.title: Wiggers diagram
heartClock.wiggers.label: Wiggers diagram: pressure in the left ventricle, aorta and left atrium, left ventricular volume and the ECG over one cardiac cycle, with a cursor at the current moment.
heartClock.wiggers.description: During ventricular systole the pressure in the left ventricle rises above the aortic pressure and blood is ejected, so the ventricular volume falls. After the aortic valve closes the pressure in the ventricle drops below the atrial pressure, the mitral valve opens and the ventricle fills again; atrial contraction adds the last part of the filling.

heartClock.inModel: How it looks in the model
heartClock.preset.normal.summary: Sinus rhythm, pressure in the aorta 120/80 mmHg, and the left ventricle ejects about two thirds of its volume on each beat.
heartClock.preset.normal.ecg: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.preset.atrial-fibrillation.su: The atria fibrillate instead of contracting: there are no P waves, the baseline shows small irregular f waves, and the intervals between beats vary without a pattern. The atria no longer add the last part of ventricular filling.
heartClock.preset.atrial-fibrillation.ec: Atrial fibrillation at an average of {rate} beats per minute. There are no P waves, the baseline shows small irregular f waves, the QRS complexes are narrow, and the intervals between them differ.
heartClock.preset.stemi.summary: The ST segment is raised by 2 mm from the J point. A diagnosis needs ST elevation in at least two contiguous leads; the model shows a single lead, similar to lead II, so it shows the inferior wall and no reciprocal changes.
heartClock.preset.stemi.ecg: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave and a narrow QRS complex; the ST segment after it is raised by 2 mm and runs into the T wave.
heartClock.preset.heart-failure: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
heartClock.preset.heart-failure.summary: The left ventricle ejects 30% of its volume on each beat instead of about two thirds; a reduced ejection fraction means 40% or less. The ECG does not change, and the model does not play the third heart sound.
heartClock.preset.heart-failure.ecg: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.preset.hypertension.summary: Blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg, above the hypertension threshold of 140/90 mmHg; NICE calls this level stage 2. The ECG does not change.
heartClock.preset.hypertension.ecg: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.preset.aortic-stenosis.summar: The aortic valve is narrowed: during ejection the pressure in the left ventricle is on average 40 mmHg higher than in the aorta, the threshold of severe stenosis. The model does not show the murmur, the slow-rising, weak pulse (pulsus parvus et tardus) or the softer second heart sound.
heartClock.preset.aortic-stenosis.ecg: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.preset.atrial-septal-defect.s: The second heart sound is split, and the split is the same on every beat. In atrial septal defect the ECG may show incomplete or complete right bundle branch block; the model only widens the QRS to the width of a complete block and does not draw its shape. Blood flows from the left atrium to the right, and the model shows only the left side of the heart, so the Wiggers diagram does not change. The model does not play the murmur.
heartClock.preset.atrial-septal-defect.e: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a wide QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.ecgDescription: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
anatomy.title: Heart anatomy
anatomy.intro: A 3D model of a normal adult heart. Rotate it, pick a structure from the list or click it on the model, make the chambers see-through or cut the heart open to look inside.
anatomy.articles: Articles on heart anatomy and function

viewer.keyboardHelp: Drag to rotate. Click the model, then scroll or pinch to zoom. With the keyboard, focus the model, then use the arrow keys to rotate, + and − to zoom, and 0 or Home to reset the view.
viewer.schematic: The conduction system is a schematic drawing: its position is approximate, placed after a published anatomical description rather than taken from the source model.
